flawed_step: The hypotheses do not imply uniqueness; strict, complete preferences can admit multiple stable matchings.
counterexample: Let n=2. Men's preferences: m1: w1>w2; m2: w2>w1. Women's preferences: w1: m2>m1; w2: m1>m2. Matching A={(m1,w1),(m2,w2)} is stable because each man has his first choice. Matching B={(m1,w2),(m2,w1)} is also stable: for unmatched pair (m1,w1), w1 prefers her partner m2; for unmatched pair (m2,w2), w2 prefers her partner m1. Thus there are two distinct stable matchings.
assessment_summary: A two-men, two-women instance with strict, complete preferences has two stable matchings, so the claimed uniqueness is false.
